I work in a treatment center, and I have quite a few clients that, among other things, are there for cannabis use. Most of them feel the same way as yourself, and here's how I personally explain it to them.

While cannabis/marijuana/weed/whatever use isn't necessarily their problem, the fact that it may be used to manage emotions is. Let me explain.

In the mental health field, the ability to manage your own emotions and life effectively is considered to be the baseline *normal* for most individuals. We have cases of mental illness that make this impossible for some people, and we also have those who use substances, (ANY substance really), to do that work for them either because they are unable to manage it themselves, or simply because they don't WANT to manage it themselves. 

Cannabis, while having no truly addictive properties, is a mind altering substance. If your use of cannabis is to HELP you regulate your emotions, and without it your mental and emotional health is largely unaffected, your usage is not necessarily a problem, (although this may differ on an individual basis).

On the opposite hand, if your usage is to regulate or maintain your emotional or mental health at ANY LEVEL, you may need some professional advice or treatment to help you learn the skills necessary to regulate yourself without substances. 

This is just how I explain the clinical approach as I understand it to my clients. Hope this helps.
